name: AutoSpec (CEGIS+ILP safety-rule evolution for LLM agents)
exact_model: arXiv:2606.24245 (method record, not a servable model)
access: public preprint (arXiv); no weights, method only
license: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license (nonexclusive-distrib); no released model weights.
context_tokens: not applicable (method record; framework around host LLM agents)
serving_path: Not servable; a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis loop guided by inductive logic programming that evolves interpretable safety rules from annotated agent traces (291 traces, F1 0.98/0.93 across two domains).
game_research_use: 2026 evidence that CEGIS-style counterexample consumption is actively applied to LLM-agent governance outside games: AutoSpec repairs the RULES from counterexample traces, whereas TRACE-RPG's guided_repair arm repairs the CANDIDATE from the validator's error set while rules and state stay frozen. Together they bracket the repair-target design space and confirm no prior work does fixture-level guided-vs-blind-vs-oracle operator comparison for game-action commit gates.
key_risk: Different repair target (rule evolution, not candidate repair) and different evidence class (F1 over annotated traces, not deterministic exact counts); citing it as direct precedent for candidate-repair efficacy would overstate the overlap.
evidence_status: verified-primary from the arXiv abstract page as of 2026-08-21.
